subject: Residency & deletion artifact inventory + audit playback
messages:
From: Claire Holt <claire.holt@northbridge.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: residency/retention/deletion artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Hi Aisha,

We're kicking off our SOC 2 fieldwork next week and the audit team has asked us to collect artifacts demonstrating retention and deletion controls for Redwood-hosted tenants. Specifically they want: 
- A sample mapping of retention TTLs by region/tenant/class of data (policy + exported mapping)
- Representative deletion logs showing the workflow from request -> queued -> executed -> verification (sanitized)
- Hash/snapshot evidence for an archived snapshot used in verification (hashlist + timestamp)
- A short chain-of-custody / playbook summary that explains the erasure orchestration (who/what/when)

Can you let me know what you can provide and an estimated timeline? For scope, they asked for a small sample (2–3 tenant IDs) plus the canonical runbook and any redaction guidance we should apply.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Holt
Senior Audit Manager | Northbridge Bank
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Holt <claire.holt@northbridge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency/retention/deletion artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a scoped sample packet and a longer evidence bundle depending on how deep the auditors need to go. Quick summary / what we'll include: 

- redwood_ttl_map_may2026.csv (exported mapping of TTLs by region and data class; includes effective dates)
- hashlist-snapshot-20260509.txt (SHA256 list for a point-in-time snapshot; timestamps included)
- sanitized-deletion-logs-tenant12345.csv (sanitized event traces showing request -> delete -> verification; tenant IDs masked except the ones you approve)
- erasure-playbook-summary.pdf (2-page executive playbook describing orchestration, roles, fallback and cross-region propagation)

Turnaround: we can produce an expedited sample packet (these four artifacts) in ~48 hours if you confirm the two tenant IDs to sample and the level of redaction you want. Full bundle (additional logs, sampling artifacts across two regions, attestation templates) will take ~5 business days because we'd need time to run the verification job and redact PII.

Next steps for us: please reply with the sample tenant IDs (or say we can select representative test tenants) and whether you want raw timestamps or converted UTC. I'll coordinate with Marcus and Vivek on the playback artifacts and with Laura for legal/attestation notes.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwood.ai]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 9 May 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: residency/retention/deletion artifacts for SOC 2 audit

Aisha / team — quick tech notes for the packet so Claire has the right expectations: 

1) Sampling & redaction: we can produce fully sanitized CSV traces where tenant identifiers are replaced with reversible tokens for audit review (token map kept in-house). If Northbridge requires original tenant IDs for matching, we need a signed NDA addendum and a list of explicit IDs.

2) Deletion log contents: the logs include event id, initiated_by (svc-account), request_time, queued_time, deletion_executed_time, verification_checksum, verification_time, region. We'll remove user content and any prompt/response payloads.

3) Cross-region propagation: for multi-region tenants we will provide proof that deletion jobs were submitted to the originating region and the downstream replication/eviction completed; that is shown by per-region deletion receipts.

4) Hashlist snapshot: generated from our immutable snapshot service; includes file path (redacted), SHA256, byte count, and snapshot_ts. If auditors want the manifest for the exact bucket objects we can provide an object manifest but recommend not sharing object keys — again, reversible tokenization is available.

5) Runbook & orchestration: summary + internal runbook (erase-playbook-v2.md) exist; the internal runbook contains internal role names and playbook flows we may want to keep redacted in the public packet. We'll provide the 2-page summary PDF and a sanitized step-by-step annex.

6) Evidence authenticity: we can provide a signed attestation (DocuSign) and an optional notarized timestamp (if required) — Laura, please confirm the attestation language.

I'll prepare the sample packet once Aisha confirms tenant IDs. Blocking items: legal signoff if original tenant IDs are requested; HSM key material never leaves our KMS and we will only share verification checksums.

-Marcus
